mechanics.name: Rooms
mechanics.summary: Room cards are split enchantments with two doors: cast either half to unlock that door, then pay the other door's mana cost as a sorcery-speed special action to fully unlock the Room. For eerie abilities, casting a Room supplies the enchantment-entry trigger up front and a second trigger when the last locked door opens.

mechanics.name: Manifest dread
mechanics.summary: Look at the top two cards of your library, put one onto the battlefield face down as a colorless 2/2 creature with no name, creature types, or abilities, and put the other into your graveyard. If the manifested card is a creature, you may turn it face up as a special action by paying its mana cost, creating both board presence and graveyard fuel.

mechanics.name: Survival
mechanics.summary: Survival abilities trigger at the beginning of your second main phase if their creature is tapped, then check that it is still tapped when the trigger resolves. Attacking, crewing, mana abilities, and other tap effects can all switch them on before that phase begins.

mechanics.name: Eerie
mechanics.summary: Each eerie ability triggers whenever an enchantment you control enters and whenever a Room you control becomes fully unlocked. A cast Room can supply the enchantment-entry trigger and, after its other door opens, one later full-unlock trigger.

mechanics.name: Impending
mechanics.summary: The five mythic Overlords may be cast for an impending cost, entering with time counters and remaining noncreature enchantments while any counters remain; remove one at the beginning of each of your end steps. Their enters abilities still trigger immediately, and removing the final counter turns them into creatures.

mechanics.name: Delirium
mechanics.summary: Delirium is active while four or more card types are represented among cards in your graveyard. Artifact creatures and enchantment creatures each supply two types, while Room is an enchantment subtype rather than another card type, so self-mill, manifest dread, and disposable mixed-type permanents are the cleanest setup.

archetypes.name: Eerie tempo
archetypes.playstyle: Curve out with enchantment creatures, Auras, and Rooms to stack eerie triggers, then turn the resulting counters and tokens into a tempo clock. Bounce or lock blockers, protect the largest threat, and remember that fully unlocking a Room supplies a second eerie trigger.

archetypes.name: Reanimator control
archetypes.playstyle: Draft this as removal-heavy control with reanimation as its finisher: loot, surveil, or landcycle oversized creatures into the graveyard, then return them without paying their additional cast costs. Prioritize time-buying interaction and recyclable value over stuffing the deck with too many expensive targets.

archetypes.name: Power-two swarm
archetypes.playstyle: Build a low curve of creatures with power 2 or less and token makers, then make every wide attack lethal through Arabella, Midnight Mayhem, attack anthems, and evasion. Cheap burn and pump should preserve tempo; avoid diluting the deck with slow cards that do not add bodies or clear blockers.

archetypes.name: Survival tap value
archetypes.playstyle: Attack when trades are favorable, but use crew, mana abilities, Coordinated Clobbering, and tap costs to turn on survival before the second main phase through stalled boards. The best builds keep a functional midrange curve and treat survival as repeatable value, not a reason to play every low-rate Survivor.

archetypes.name: Eerie attrition
archetypes.playstyle: Stabilize with enchantment-based removal and Rooms, using each enchantment entry or fully unlocked Room to convert eerie into surveil, cards, drain, or recursive threats. Win by compounding small advantages behind blockers and instant-speed interaction rather than racing.

archetypes.name: Room value control
archetypes.playstyle: Use early doors as modular removal, tempo, and card selection, then spend spare mana unlocking their late halves while holding the board. Preserve high-impact Rooms for cumulative value and cash in exhausted ones only when Intruding Soulrager's card and damage justify shrinking Smoky Lounge // Misty Salon.

archetypes.name: Manifest dread value
archetypes.playstyle: Manifest dread converts card selection into board presence while Oblivious Bookworm, Paranormal Analyst, and Threats Around Every Corner recoup the setup with cards or mana. Favor creatures worth turning face up, represent combat flips, and win through incremental advantage plus oversized manifested threats.

archetypes.name: Sacrifice value grind
archetypes.playstyle: Convert expendable creatures and used-up Auras or Rooms into removal, cards, and drain, while keeping outlets and fodder in balance. Trade repeatedly, pressure with menace between exchanges, and win by chaining death value rather than racing.

archetypes.name: Delirium attrition control
archetypes.playstyle: Use surveil, manifest dread, and self-mill to assemble four card types while trading through the early game. Once delirium is online, discounted removal, recurring threats, and attrition engines dominate; prioritize diverse types, especially artifact and enchantment creatures, over redundant filler.

archetypes.name: Delirium beatdown
archetypes.playstyle: Curve out with artifact and enchantment creatures that contribute multiple graveyard types, then switch on delirium and attack with upgraded threats. Creatures, lands, and sorceries arrive naturally, so prioritize cheap artifacts, enchantments, and instants without sacrificing pressure.

combos.note: Glimmer triggers Tamer on entry and discounts every later enchantment or unlock.
Dancers unlocks the Room's second door to trigger its own eerie ability and create a 3/1 Spirit.
Glimmerburst's enchantment token triggers Tamer to create an extra Gremlin.
Commune stocks a creature for Rite to reanimate and can mill Rite for its flashback cost.
Rite reanimates Shroudstomper and immediately triggers its drain, life gain, and card draw.
Each Shroudstomper life-gain trigger makes Enduring Tenacity drain the opponent for 2 more.
Mayhem's three 1/1s add three to Arabella's attack-trigger damage and life gain.
Enduring Courage turns Mayhem's three Gremlins into hasty 3/1s for the turn.
Crewing Hovership taps Storyteller for its second-main survival trigger without risking it in combat.
Tyvar taps Storyteller as its indestructible cost to guarantee Storyteller's survival trigger.
Fear returns a spent Nowhere to Run as its extra cost so the -3/-3 entry effect can be replayed.
Fear returning itself from the graveyard triggers Defiled Crypt to create a Horror.
Soulrager cashes a fully unlocked Meat Locker into 2 damage and a card after both one-shot doors resolve.
Fear returns Glassworks after its 4-damage door resolves so that door can be cast again.
A Keybearer hit unlocks Misty Salon for free to create its unlocked-door-sized Spirit.
Grasp's manifest satisfies Bookworm's end-step condition to turn its loot into a clean draw.
Grasp's manifest triggers Threats to put a basic land onto the battlefield tapped.
Shrieker turns a manifested creature face up for {1}{G}, triggering Growing Dread's counter.
Final Vengeance sacrifices Mirth for its cost, triggering Mirth's manifest before the creature is exiled.
Possession steals a creature that Final Vengeance can sacrifice while exiling a second target.
Skinripper sacrifices Percussionist to grow, enable its end-step damage, and expose the next card to play.
At delirium, Swarmweaver gives Broodspinner and all the Insects it creates +1/+1 and deathtouch.
Under the Skin's graveyard return triggers Defiled Crypt to create a Horror alongside the manifest.
At delirium, Fear untaps Wickerfolk after its first attack so the hasty trampler can attack again.
At delirium, Rollercrusher doubles the damage Beastie Beatdown's boosted creature deals.
